claims.text: A functionally graded interlayer between W and CuCrZr will reduce interfacial thermal stresses.
A functionally graded interlayer between W and CuCrZr will improve joint integrity under fusion-reactor conditions.
A Ni-based alloy is a suitable ductile, intermediate-CTE interlayer material for W/CuCrZr joints.
A Mo-based alloy is an alternative suitable interlayer material for W/CuCrZr joints.
Directly joined W and CuCrZr have a large thermal-expansion mismatch.
The thermal-expansion mismatch in directly joined W/CuCrZr produces residual stresses during extreme thermal cycling.
The proposed interlayer is thin and functionally graded, transitioning from a composition near W toward a Ni-based alloy.
The graded interlayer can be produced by diffusion bonding or advanced deposition techniques.
Fusion-reactor materials encounter high temperature, high heat flux, and irradiation.
The graded interlayer progressively bridges the CTE mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A gradual change in material properties accommodates differential thermal expansion.
Accommodation of differential thermal expansion reduces mechanical stress at the W/CuCrZr interface.
Reduced interfacial mechanical stress enhances bonding during rapid thermal cycling and irradiation.
The graded interlayer will measurably reduce interfacial stresses relative to direct bonding.
The graded interlayer will improve joint mechanical integrity and durability under fusion-relevant conditions relative to direct bonding.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonds are prone to failure because thermal-expansion mismatch produces high interfacial stresses.
Interlayer effectiveness depends on thickness, compositional-gradient precision, and processing method.
Failure to optimize interlayer parameters may make thermal-stress mitigation insufficient during prolonged extreme exposure.
